title: Interface model
description: What exists outside a document: addresses the platform owns, the names prose uses for them, and the values each may take. Supplied by a pack; the authoring core never carries one.

address.description: The platform's own identifier. Opaque to the core.

role.description: input: the document receives it. output: the document writes it. internal: the platform owns it and the document may read it, but it is not a subject-matter input. upstream: ANOTHER SPECIFICATION IN THE SAME SYSTEM WRITES IT -- this document reads it and does not decide it. Measured 2026-09-20 over 129 subject packs against a 244-component platform: of 180 addresses the examples drove and the packs did not declare, 45 are output by another component, and they are CONCENTRATED -- 19 of one pack's 20 and 9 of another's 9, against 2 of the largest pack's 33. Without this value such an address is simply absent, which reads as a specification reaching outside what it declares; with it the tool can say the true thing instead, which is that one specification is not one program and the author has another document to go and read.

names.description: What prose calls this address. A list because prose is inconsistent. This is the only place the correspondence is written down. ⚠ LIST EVERY SPELLING THE PLATFORM KNOWS, INCLUDING THE ADDRESS'S OWN LAST SEGMENT WHEN THAT IS ONE -- and do not trim the list to the spellings some particular document happens to use. Trimming was measured and it buys nothing: the reader's notion of 'mentioned' is a disjunction over these, so removing a name it already answers False for cannot move any question, and over 129 packs, eleven classes and three differently-built models it moved ZERO of 2,109. What DOES move is the last segment being present or absent, because the partition that cuts a document into one block per subject awards a line to the longest spelling written on it: measured 2026-09-20, publishing every spelling rather than the used ones changes 4 findings in 2 of 129 packs, always where one address carries fifteen spellings and takes a line from a neighbour that carries one. That is 0.19%, and the price of an interface model that is a property of the PLATFORM -- written once, published, and read by every specification since -- rather than an artefact that has to be rebuilt for each document.

values.description: For a scalar address. Mutually exclusive with fields.

type.description: For a scalar address with no enumerated values. `integer` when the platform holds only whole numbers there, `number` when it holds fractions or does not say. The difference reaches the platform: a fraction landed where it keeps an integer is a value it cannot hold, and measured 2026-09-26 a skeleton that could only say `number` declared a count as float64 and the component it fed could not be connected.

fields.description: For a record address. Each field carries its own value space.

allOf.$comment: A scalar address and a record address are different shapes; carrying both hides which one a writer meant.

valueSpace.description: Symbol to number. The numbers are the platform's; the core compares symbols and passes numbers through untouched.
